## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 None of the secondary literature matches discuss Kv 4.4 directly, as the retrieved search results merely attest to the widespread use of the standard grammatical participle *samannāgata* ("endowed with") across disparate sutta, vinaya, and commentarial contexts.

Textual reuse analyses generated by DharmaNexus show substantial structural and formulaic parallels across the Pali canon, registering 1,346 matching passages across 41 texts, mostly within the *Kathāvatthu* itself [DharmaNexus]. By far its most extensive reuse partner is the *Aparāpisamannāgatakathā* (Kv 4.9), which shares 436 passages and 53,841 characters, with an especially dense alignment between Kv 4.4 §5.7–17.3 and Kv 4.9 §8.3–20.3 [DharmaNexus]. Other major intra-textual connections include the *Parihānikathā* (Kv 1.2), the *Dvīhisīlehikathā* (Kv 10.6), the *Upekkhāsamannāgatakathā* (Kv 4.5), and the *Atītānāgatasamannāgatakathā* (Kv 9.11) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects low-scoring automated alignments with Tibetan translations of Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4091) and the *Karmaśataka* (D0340-2) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
